newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower on South America crop.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower on South America crop.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed lower on persistent references to the near-ideal crop weather in South America, traders said.
"South American weather is the key and it's beautiful," a trader said.
The South American soybean crop is being planted on schedule and soil moisture levels remain at satisfactory levels, the traders said.
Brazilian soybean seedings as of December 5 were 83 percent complete, ahead of 78 percent a year ago and only slightly behind the 84 percent average pace.
The soy complex also was hit be follow through from the bearish close Monday and commercial selling in soymeal which led to talk China may have cancelled orders for U.S. soymeal, traders said.

But there were several traders who said the drop in nearby soymeal was tied to a decline in spot cash soymeal basis levels and a building inventory of soymeal available for export and domestic use. The soybean crush pace has been occuring at record levels and exports have slowed.
Soybeans closed 1/2 to eight cents per bushel lower, with January down 3-3/4 at $6.85.
Lee B. Stern and Co, Griffin Trading and Cargill Inc each sold two million bushels of March, traders said, while ADM Investor Services bought two million bushels of March.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 50,000 contracts, slightly above the 49,491 traded Monday.
In soybean options, Smith Barney bought 500 March $7.50 calls and sold 500 March $7.00 calls at 8-1/2 cents and LIT AMerica sold 400 January $6.75 puts at three to four cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 11,000 contracts, above the 9,038 traded Monday.
